app.name: Data readiness check
home.title: Check a dataset of data.gov.gr
home.lead: Paste its address. Nine checks on the metadata show what is fine and what to fix, so that the data are easier to use, also by artificial intelligence systems.
home.opinion: Optional after the check: a second opinion from an AI model
form.label: Address of the dataset
form.loading: Reading the metadata from the portal…
form.preparing: The check is being prepared. The first time takes a few seconds.
how.title: How it works
how.1.title: Copy the address
how.1.text: Open the dataset on data.gov.gr and copy the address from the address bar of the browser.
how.2.title: Press “Check”
how.2.text: The application reads the metadata of the dataset from the portal. It does not download its files.
how.3.title: Read what was found
how.3.text: For each check, the page shows whether it is met, partly met or not met, and what to change on the portal.
how.4.title: Go through the checklist
how.4.text: Fourteen criteria need the files or human judgement. They are shown as questions, to be checked by hand.
legend.title: What the marks mean
legend.partly: Something is missing or needs a correction.
legend.not_measured: The metadata are not enough for an answer.
know.title: Good to know
know.1: The tool is free to use and needs no account.
know.2: Only the metadata that are already public on the portal are read. No file of the dataset is downloaded and nothing is stored.
know.3: The result is indicative. It is not an official assessment of the dataset or of its publisher.
know.4: The tool is independent. It does not belong to data.gov.gr.
footer.credit: Tool of the study “Quality and AI readiness of the open data of data.gov.gr”, an internship of the MSc in e-Governance of the University of the Aegean at GFOSS. Assessment criteria, version {criteria_version}.
footer.disclaimer: The result is indicative and is not an official assessment. The tool is independent and does not belong to data.gov.gr. Assessment criteria, version {criteria_version}.

group.intro: The study places every dataset in one of three groups: “Ready”, “Almost ready”, “Not yet”. Six core criteria decide the group, and three of them are visible here: title and description, licence, file format.
group.below: Not yet met: {names}. Until they are corrected, the dataset cannot be called “Ready”.
group.below.one: Not yet met: {names}. Until it is corrected, the dataset cannot be called “Ready”.
group.all_met: All three are met. Whether the dataset is “Ready” depends on the other three core criteria.
group.rest: The other three core criteria (availability, structure, documentation) are in the checklist.
fix.title: What to fix first
fix.none: The metadata checks found nothing to correct. See also the checklist.
effort_long.Low: Usually low effort: only the metadata change.
effort_long.Medium: Usually medium effort: a new file or a new link is needed.
checks.title: The nine checks
checks.intro: “Score by rule” means that the result comes from the rule alone. “Proposal” means that a person had better look at it too. The word “files” stands for everything the dataset offers: files, links and services.
checks.group.availability: The way the data are offered
code.title: Criterion {id}: how it is scored (opens in a new tab)
codes.note: The code before every name, e.g. M1, is the code of the criterion in the study. Press it to see, in a new tab, how the criterion is scored.
details.rules: All the scores of criterion {id}, on the page {page}
reading.title: AI second opinion
reading.offer.title: A second opinion from an AI model
reading.offer.lead: An artificial intelligence model, Jev, reads the description of the dataset and, where the portal gives them, the names of its columns. It notes what they state and what they do not, from what the data contain to how accurate they are, and which category of high-value datasets they seem to belong to.
reading.offer.sent: Only the title, the description, the descriptions of the resources and the names of the columns with the data dictionary are sent, all already public on the portal. No record of the data.
reading.offer.key_use: The key is used for this reading only and is not stored.
reading.offer.scores: No score changes. Without a key, the nine checks work as before.
reading.offer.terms: What happens to the key and to the texts
reading.offer.help: No key yet? See how to get one
reading.waiting: The model is reading the description…
reading.result.title: What the description states
reading.result.lead: The model read the title, the description, the descriptions of the resources and, where there were any, the names of the columns. For every statement it gives how likely it is to hold, from 0 to 1.
reading.row.coverage: Names the area, the period or the cases covered
reading.row.collection: Says where the data come from or how they were collected
reading.row.errors: Says how accurate the data are
reading.row.frequency: Says how often they are updated
reading.row.personal: Says whether they hold personal data
reading.row.names: The names of the columns are understandable without a dictionary
reading.row.hvd_category: Which category of high-value datasets they seem to belong to
reading.advice.title: What could be added or improved
reading.advice.none: The description seems to state everything asked. No addition is proposed.
reading.advice.contents: What the data contain: what each record holds and which details it gives.
reading.advice.coverage: Which area, which period and which cases the data cover.
reading.advice.gaps: What is not included or which values are missing.
reading.advice.collection: Where the data come from and how they are collected.
reading.advice.errors: How accurate the data are and whether the way of recording has changed.
reading.advice.frequency: How often the data are updated, e.g. “Updated every month”, or that they will not be updated.
reading.advice.personal: Whether the data concern persons and how they are protected, e.g. “Totals by municipality, with no personal data”.
reading.advice.fields: A data dictionary: for every column, what it holds, in which unit and what its codes mean.
reading.advice.names: Names of columns that say what they hold, or their explanation in the data dictionary.
reading.note.texts: The reading concerns only the texts of the metadata. What is stated in a document or on a page of the publisher does not show here.
reading.note.scores: The proposal changes no score and may be wrong. On the questions about limitations the model says “yes” more easily than the study: an “Unlikely” is more certain than a “Likely”.
reading.note.new: The questions for the criteria M2, M8, AI2 and M9 were added on 20/11/2026 and, unlike the others, have not yet been compared with human judgement.
reading.note.no_columns: The portal gave no names of columns for this dataset, so the question on the names of the columns was not asked.
reading.hvd.likely: The texts look like a dataset of the category “{category}” ({figure}).
reading.hvd.none: The texts look like none of the six categories ({figure}).
reading.hvd.unclear: The texts show no category clearly; the likeliest is “{category}” ({figure}).
reading.hvd.unmarked: The dataset has no high-value designation in its metadata. If it belongs to the category, the designation is missing.
reading.hvd.disclaimer: A hint from the texts: it does not judge whether the dataset is high-value or whether it meets Regulation (EU) 2023/138.
reading.error.key_missing: Type your key for Jev first.
reading.error.key: The key was not accepted. Check that the whole key was copied, without spaces, and that it is active.
reading.error.limit: Jev accepts no more requests right now. Try again in a minute.
reading.error.service: The reading was not made. Jev did not answer or the connection was lost. Try again in a few minutes.
reading.error.engine: The reading did not start in this browser. Reload the page and try again.
opinion.title: AI second opinion
opinion.heading: A second opinion from an AI model
opinion.lead: After the check, an artificial intelligence model, Jev, reads the description of the dataset and, where the portal gives them, the names of its columns, and answers up to ten questions. It gives no score and needs your own key.
opinion.steps.title: How it goes
opinion.step.1.title: Check the dataset
opinion.step.1.text: Paste its address in the field. The nine checks run as always, without a key.
opinion.step.2.title: Give your key
opinion.step.2.text: In the tab {tab} of the result, type your key for Jev and press {button}.
opinion.step.3.title: Read the answers and the hint
opinion.step.3.text: Every question gets {likely}, {unsure} or {unlikely}, and a note on what could be added to the description.
opinion.need.title: What is needed
opinion.need.key: A key for Jev. TypeSafe AI issues it to the holder of an account.
opinion.trust.title: How far to trust it
opinion.trust.lead: The second opinion is the suggestion of a model and can be wrong.
opinion.how.title: How Jev works
opinion.how.model: Jev is an artificial intelligence model of the company TypeSafe AI. It writes no text: it reads the texts it is given and, for every statement it is asked to judge, answers with a number from 0 to 1, how likely the statement is to be true. For a question with options it gives such a number for every option.
opinion.how.sent: The page sends it the title, the description and the descriptions of the resources of the dataset and, where the portal gives them, the names of the columns with the data dictionary, for up to three tables. It also sends up to nine statements, each with when it is true and when it is not, and one question with options on the six categories of high-value datasets. The first statement is: “The description of the dataset tells a reader what the data contain.”
opinion.how.bands: The page shows the number and a word: from {likely} upwards {likely_word}, up to {unlikely} {unlikely_word} and in between {unsure_word}.
opinion.how.scores: Jev gives no score and changes none of the nine checks. Its answer is a proposal and can be wrong.
opinion.how.criteria: The questions belong to six criteria of the study:
opinion.key.title: How to get a key
opinion.key.lead: The key is issued by TypeSafe AI, the company of Jev, to the holder of an account in its console. The application issues no keys.
opinion.key.step.1: Open the console of TypeSafe AI at {link} and sign in to your account.
opinion.key.step.2: Press “API Keys” in the menu on the left.
opinion.key.step.3: Press “Create key”, top right, and copy the new key.
opinion.key.step.4: Paste it in the field {field}, in the tab {tab} of the result, and press {button}.
opinion.key.care: The key is yours, like a password: do not publish it and do not give it to others. The page does not store it, so it is pasted again for every new reading.
opinion.key.cost: TypeSafe AI charges the use to your account, according to the size of the texts that the model reads.
opinion.key.figure: A sketch of the console, not a picture of it. 2 marks “API Keys” in the menu on the left and 3 marks “Create key” top right.
checklist.title: What is not checked automatically
checklist.intro: The following 14 criteria of the study need the files themselves or human judgement. The application gives them no score. They are to be checked by hand. The boxes are for personal use only and are not stored.
checklist.Q1.question: Can all the files be downloaded and opened?
checklist.Q1.if_not: Correct the link or upload the file again.
checklist.Q1.name: File availability
checklist.AI1.question: Can a program read the files, without cleaning by hand?
checklist.AI1.if_not: Restructure the file, so that it reads as a table.
checklist.AI1.name: Structure a program can read
checklist.Q2.question: Are few values missing, under 5% of the cells?
checklist.Q2.if_not: Complete the file or state why values are missing.
checklist.Q2.name: Completeness
checklist.Q3.question: Are the values written in the same way everywhere?
checklist.Q3.if_not: Harmonise the way values are written in the files.
checklist.Q3.name: Consistency
checklist.Q4.question: Are the values plausible?
checklist.Q4.if_not: Correct the values. If the error comes from the system that produces them, correct it there.
checklist.Q4.name: Plausible values
checklist.AI6.question: Are there common codes or coordinates, for joining with other data?
checklist.AI6.name: Linkage through common codes
checklist.AI2.question: Is the meaning of every field explained, with its unit and its codes?
checklist.AI2.name: Documentation of the structure
checklist.M5.question: Are the data offered free of charge and without registration?
checklist.M5.if_not: A change in the access policy of the publisher is needed.
checklist.M5.name: Free access
checklist.M8.question: Is the exposure of personal data avoided?
checklist.M8.if_not: Remove these fields or give them in aggregate form.
checklist.M8.name: Personal data
checklist.M10.question: Is there both an API and a bulk download? For high-value datasets only.
checklist.M10.if_not: Offer a complete download of the data and, if missing, an API.
checklist.M10.name: API and bulk download
checklist.AI3.question: Are earlier periods or versions of the data available?
checklist.AI3.if_not: Publish the archive of the earlier periods.
checklist.AI3.name: Historical depth
checklist.AI4.question: Can the dataset be described in Croissant or with a datasheet?
checklist.AI4.if_not: Complete the metadata and the data dictionary.
checklist.AI4.name: Description in Croissant or a datasheet
checklist.AI5.question: Can the content be split into self-contained pieces that an AI system can retrieve and cite?
checklist.AI5.if_not: Publish the content as structured text or as records.
checklist.AI5.name: Suitability for retrieval (RAG)
checklist.AI7.question: Are the known limitations of the data stated?
checklist.AI7.if_not: Add a short note on the limitations.
checklist.AI7.name: Declared limitations
download.note: The Excel file is in the language of the page, in plain words. The Markdown and JSON files are technical.
download.failed: The file was not prepared. Try again.
error.title: The check was not made
error.empty: No address was given. Paste the address of a dataset, e.g. https://data.gov.gr/dataset/troxaia-atyxhmata.
error.other_site: The address is not on data.gov.gr. Open the dataset on data.gov.gr and copy the address from the address bar of the browser.
error.not_dataset_page: The address is on data.gov.gr, but it is not the page of a dataset. The address of a dataset starts with https://data.gov.gr/dataset/ and continues with its name.
error.not_a_name: This does not look like the address of a dataset. Paste the whole address, e.g. https://data.gov.gr/dataset/troxaia-atyxhmata.
error.not_found: No dataset was found at this address. Check that the whole address was copied and that the dataset is public.
error.record.data-service: The address leads to a data service of the portal, not to a dataset. The criteria apply to datasets only.
error.record.decision: The address leads to a decision published on the portal, not to a dataset. The criteria apply to datasets only.
error.record.other: This record is not a dataset. The criteria apply to datasets only.
error.portal: The portal data.gov.gr did not answer. Try again in a few minutes. If this goes on, see whether the portal itself opens.
error.engine: The check did not start in this browser. Reload the page. If it goes on, try a recent version of Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
missing.title: Page not found
missing.text: The address matches no page of the tool.
common.no_resources: The dataset has no file or link.
common.no_resources_action: Add the data to the dataset, as a file or as a link.
common.no_resources_fix: Add the data to the dataset.
common.no_address: No file of the dataset has an address.
common.address_action: Fill in the address (URL) of every file.
common.address_fix: Fill in the addresses of the files.
generic.finding.not_measured: The metadata are not enough for an answer.
generic.action: See in the details the reason given by the check and the rule of the criterion.
check.M1.title: Title and description
check.M1.why: The title and the description are the first thing read by anyone looking for data, person or program. Without them the dataset is not found and not understood.
check.M2.title: Supporting details
check.M2.why: Keywords, theme, coverage and frequency help people find the dataset and judge whether it fits a use.
check.M3.title: Standard terms
check.M3.why: Standard terms are the same across Europe. They let the dataset be filtered correctly on the portal and on data.europa.eu.
check.M9.title: High-value marking
check.M9.why: High-value datasets carry extra obligations under Regulation (EU) 2023/138. The marking shows which ones they are.
check.Q5.title: Timeliness
check.Q5.why: Anyone who uses the data has to know how recent they are and when they will be renewed.
check.M4.title: Licence
check.M4.why: Without a clear open licence nobody knows whether the data may be used.
check.M6.title: How the data are offered
check.M6.why: With a direct link or an API the data are obtained automatically, without pages in between.
check.M7.title: Stable addresses
check.M7.why: If the address of a file changes, those who use it or refer to it lose it.
check.Q6.title: File format
check.Q6.why: An open, structured format is read by every program, without the software of one vendor.
m1.ok: There is a title and a description with content, and every file has an access address.
m1.ok_no_resources: There is a title and a description with content. The dataset, however, has no file or link.
m1.without_url: {n} of the {resources} files have no access address.
m1.without_url.one: 1 of the {resources} files has no access address.
m1.repeats_title: The description repeats the title and says nothing more.
m1.short_description: The description is very short: {chars} characters, while at least {minimum} are needed.
m1.action_description: Write in the description what the data contain: what they measure, for which period and for which area.
m1.action_title: Give the dataset a title that says what it contains.
m2.all: All 7 are filled in: keywords, theme, publisher, contact point, geographical coverage, temporal coverage, update frequency.
m2.partial: {present} of the 7 details are filled in. Without a value: {missing}.
m2.partial.one: 1 of the 7 details is filled in. Without a value: {missing}.
m2.none: None of the 7 details is filled in: {missing}.
m2.action: Fill in what is missing in the form of the portal.
m2.fix: Fill in the details missing from the description of the dataset.
m3.all_vocab: Everything that is declared (theme, update frequency, file format) is written with terms of the catalogue.
m3.free_formats: In {n} of the {with_format} files that declare a format, the format is typed freely ({values}) and not with a term of the catalogue.
m3.free_theme: The theme is not written with a term of the catalogue.
m3.free_frequency: The update frequency is not written with a term of the catalogue.
m3.no_vocab: Nothing of what is declared (theme, update frequency, file format) is written with a term of the catalogue.
m3.nothing_declared: No theme, update frequency or file format is declared.
m3.action_formats: In the form of the portal, pick the format from the list instead of typing it.
m3.action_terms: Pick the theme and the update frequency from the lists of the form.
m3.action_declare: Declare a theme, an update frequency and a file format, picking them from the lists of the form.
m3.fix_formats: Pick the format of the files from the list of the portal.
m3.fix_terms: Pick the theme and the frequency from the lists of the portal.
m4.open: All the files carry the same open licence, {licence}.
m4.open.one: The file carries an open licence, {licence}.
m4.share_alike: The licence {licence} is open, but it requires whatever is made from the data to be offered under the same licence.
m4.text_only: The licence is given only as text, without a link to the licence itself.
m4.restrictive: At least one file carries a licence that restricts re-use ({licences}).
m4.missing_some: {n} of the {resources} files declare no licence.
m4.missing_some.one: 1 of the {resources} files declares no licence.
m4.unclassed: The licence {licence} is not recognised automatically and needs a check by a person.
m4.action_declare: In the form of the portal, pick an open licence from the list for every file, e.g. CC BY 4.0.
m4.action_restrictive: If the publisher can, change the licence to an open one, e.g. CC BY 4.0. Changing the licence is a decision of the publisher.
m4.action_share_alike: If there is no reason for this condition, prefer CC BY 4.0.
m4.action_different: Declare the same licence for all the files.
m4.action_unclassed: Check that the licence allows free re-use.
m4.fix_declare: Declare an open licence for every file.
m4.fix_restrictive: Consider whether the licence can become open.
m4.fix_share_alike: Consider whether the licence can become CC BY 4.0.
m4.fix_different: Declare the same licence for all the files.
m6.file_all: All {resources} files are downloaded through a direct link.
m6.file_all.one: The file is downloaded through a direct link.
m6.file_some: {n} of the {resources} files are downloaded through a direct link.
m6.file_some.one: 1 of the {resources} files is downloaded through a direct link.
m6.api: The data are offered through an API or a data service ({n} of the {resources} files).
m6.map_only: The data are shown only as a map (WMS service). There is no file or service that gives the data themselves.
m6.pages_only: The links of the dataset lead only to web pages, not to a file or a data service.
m6.note_unverified: This follows only from the declared format and was not verified.
m6.action_map: Add a file for download or a service that gives the data, e.g. WFS.
m6.action_pages: Upload the file on the portal or give a direct link to it.
m6.fix_map: Offer the data themselves too, not only the map.
m6.fix_pages: Give a direct link to the data.
m7.stable_portal: The dataset has a permanent identifier, and its {resources} files are uploaded on the portal, with a stable address.
m7.stable_portal.one: The dataset has a permanent identifier, and its file is uploaded on the portal, with a stable address.
m7.stable: The dataset has a permanent identifier, and all its files have a stable address.
m7.all_changing: All the files are offered through an address that changes: with a temporary code, a shortened link or a redirect.
m7.some_changing: {n} of the {resources} files are offered through an address that changes: with a temporary code, a shortened link or a redirect.
m7.some_changing.one: 1 of the {resources} files is offered through an address that changes: with a temporary code, a shortened link or a redirect.
m7.missing_some: {n} of the {resources} files have no address.
m7.missing_some.one: 1 of the {resources} files has no address.
m7.action_changing: Replace these links with permanent addresses, or upload the files on the portal.
m9.full: The dataset is declared as high-value, in the category “{categories}”, with a reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138.
m9.category_only: A high-value category is declared (“{categories}”), but the reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138 is missing.
m9.regulation_only: There is a reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138, but no high-value category is declared.
m9.type_only: The dataset has only the type “high-value dataset”, without a category and without a reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138.
m9.not_judged: The dataset has no high-value marking. The metadata do not show whether its content falls under the high-value categories, so the check gives no result.
m9.action_complete: Fill in both the high-value category and the reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138 in the form of the portal.
m9.action_not_judged: If the data fall under one of the six categories of Regulation (EU) 2023/138 (geospatial, earth observation and environment, meteorological, statistics, companies, mobility), declare the category and the Regulation in the form. Otherwise nothing needs to be done.
m9.fix_complete: Complete the high-value marking: category and Regulation.
q5.static_with_period: The dataset is declared as not updated, and the title or the description says which period the data cover.
q5.lead_periodic: The dataset is declared as updated {frequency}.
q5.lead_static: The dataset is declared as not updated, but neither the title nor the description says which period the data cover.
q5.lead_none: No update frequency with a definite period is declared.
q5.on_time: The last upload was {days} ago, within the limits of this frequency.
q5.late: The last upload was {days} ago: it is late compared with the declared frequency.
q5.very_late: The last upload was {days} ago: the delay exceeds three update periods.
q5.old: The last upload was {days} ago, more than a year.
q5.not_measurable: The portal has no upload date for the files of the dataset, so timeliness cannot be measured from the metadata.
q5.action_period: Write the period of the data in the title or in the description. If the dataset is updated, declare the actual frequency.
q5.action_frequency: Declare in the form of the portal how often the dataset is updated. If it will not be updated, declare that and write the period of the data in the description.
q5.action_update: Upload the newest data. If the dataset is updated less often, declare the actual frequency.
q5.action_check: Check by hand whether the data are up to date.
q5.fix_period: Write which period the data cover.
q5.fix_update: Upload the newest data or correct the declared frequency.
q6.open: The data are also offered in an open, structured format ({n} of the {resources} files).
q6.excel_only: The data are offered only in Excel ({resources} files), which is the format of one vendor.
q6.excel_only.one: The data are offered only in Excel (1 file), which is the format of one vendor.
q6.vendor: The most open format of the dataset is structured but belongs to one vendor, such as Excel or Shapefile ({n} of the {resources} files).
q6.unstructured: The data are offered only in a form that a program does not read as a table, such as PDF, a text document, a web page or a map.
q6.undetermined: The format cannot be told from the metadata, e.g. because the files are compressed or declare no format.
q6.note_provisional: The result is provisional: {n} compressed files with unknown content could improve it.
q6.note_provisional.one: The result is provisional: 1 compressed file with unknown content could improve it.
q6.action_open: Upload the same data in an open format too, e.g. CSV, next to the existing file.
q6.action_open_excel: Upload the same data in an open format too, e.g. CSV, next to the Excel file.
q6.action_structured: Upload the data as a table in an open format too, e.g. CSV, next to the existing file.
q6.action_declare: Declare the format of every file, and prefer an open format, e.g. CSV.
q6.fix_open: Upload the data in an open format too, e.g. CSV.
guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: The tool reads the metadata of a dataset of data.gov.gr, that is, what the page of the dataset on the portal says: title, description, licence, files. It makes nine checks and says in plain words what to fix.
guide.steps.title: The four steps
guide.read.title: How to read the result
guide.read.marks: Every check has a mark and a word: Met, Partly, Not met or Not measured.
guide.read.kinds: “Score by rule” means that the result comes from the rule alone and needs no confirmation. “Proposal” means that the check sees only the metadata, so a person had better have a look too.
guide.read.core: A “core criterion” is one of the six criteria that decide whether a dataset is ready. Fix these first.
guide.read.details: The code before the name of every check, e.g. M1, is the code of the criterion in the study. The “Details” give the score from 0 to 2, the reason of the check and the rule of the score. All the rules, for every criterion, are on the page {page}.
guide.reading.title: The AI second opinion
guide.reading.text: In the tab “AI second opinion” of the result, a second reading of the description can be asked from Jev, an artificial intelligence model of the company TypeSafe AI. It is optional and needs your own key, which TypeSafe AI issues to the holder of an account. The model reads only the title, the description and the descriptions of the resources and, where the portal gives them, the names of the columns with the data dictionary. It answers up to ten questions: whether the texts say what the data contain, how often they are updated, whether they hold personal data, what each column holds, what they cover, what is missing, where they come from and how accurate they are, whether the names of the columns are understandable, and which category of high-value datasets they seem to belong to. For each statement it gives a probability from 0 to 1: from {likely} upwards it writes “Likely”, up to {unlikely} “Unlikely” and in between “Unsure”. It gives no score and changes none.
guide.reading.trial: The model was tried on the 36 datasets of the sample of the study. On the four questions about limitations, every “Unlikely” of the model (88 answers) was a “no” in the reading of the study too. Of its 39 “Likely”, 29 were a “yes” in the study. So the model says “yes” more easily: an “Unlikely” deserves to be taken seriously, while a “Likely” is worth checking by hand. The same description may get slightly different values in two readings. The questions for the criteria M2, M8, AI2 and M9 were added after the trial and have not been tried yet.
guide.after.title: What to do next
guide.after.text: Make the changes in the form of the dataset on the portal and press “Check” again. Keep the report in Excel to share it.
guide.limits.title: What it does not do
guide.limits.text: It does not download or open the files of the dataset. This is why fourteen criteria get no score and are shown as questions, to be checked by hand. The result is indicative and not an official assessment.
guide.words.title: Words used on the page
guide.words.metadata: Metadata: the information that describes a dataset, not the data themselves. Example: the title “Road accidents” and the licence are metadata; the numbers of accidents are the data.
guide.words.format: Format: the kind of file. Example: CSV is an open format that every program reads; XLSX is the format of Excel.
guide.words.licence: Licence: the terms under which the data may be used. Example: CC BY 4.0 allows every use, with a mention of the source.
guide.words.hvd: High-value dataset: a dataset that falls under one of the six categories of Regulation (EU) 2023/138, e.g. statistics or geospatial data, and carries extra obligations on how it is offered.
terms.title: Terms of use and data
terms.updated: Terms of use, version 2, November 2026. This text is not legal advice.
terms.what.title: What the tool is
terms.what.text: The tool was made for the study “Quality and AI readiness of the open data of data.gov.gr”, which is carried out in the MSc in e-Governance of the University of the Aegean. The page is run by Michail Skandalidis, who built it during his internship at GFOSS. The page is not a service of GFOSS or of data.gov.gr. It is independent: it belongs to no public service and expresses no official position of any body.
terms.result.title: What the result is worth
terms.result.text: The result is produced automatically, from the metadata alone, and is indicative. It may be wrong or incomplete. It is not an official assessment of the dataset or of its publisher and does not replace a check by a person.
terms.use.title: Use
terms.use.text: The tool is free to use and needs no account. The page checks one dataset at a time. For many datasets together there is the command of the repository.
terms.data.title: Which data are read
terms.data.text: The check runs inside your browser. The page asks data.gov.gr for the public metadata of the dataset, with one call to the public interface (API) of the portal and under its terms of use. If the browser cannot call the portal directly, the call goes through the server that hosts the page, which passes it on and keeps nothing. No file of the dataset is downloaded. The application keeps no history of the checks, uses no tracking or advertising cookies and sends nothing to third parties, except for the AI second opinion described below, when it is asked for. The provider that hosts the page may keep technical logs, as every website does.
terms.reading.title: Second opinion from an AI model
terms.reading.text: The AI second opinion is a second reading of the description by a model. It is optional and happens only when it is asked for, with your own key for Jev, an artificial intelligence model of the company TypeSafe AI. The page then sends to TypeSafe AI the title, the description and the descriptions of the resources of the dataset and, where the portal gives them, the names of the columns with their types and data dictionary, all already public on data.gov.gr, together with your key. For the names of the columns the page asks the portal only for the structure of the tables, without any row. No record of the data is sent. The request goes through the server that hosts the page, which passes it on without keeping the key or the texts. The page stores the key nowhere and writes it in no report. The use of the key is charged to your own account at TypeSafe AI, and what the company receives is subject to its own terms. The answer is a proposal of a model: it may be wrong, it is not a score and it changes no score.
terms.personal.title: Personal data
terms.personal.text: The tool asks for no personal details. It does not show or store records of any dataset, nor the contact details given in the metadata.
terms.licences.title: Licences
terms.licences.text: The code is open, under the EUPL 1.2 licence, in the repository HermesLogios/datagovgr-ai-readiness on GitHub. The page uses the typeface Manrope (SIL Open Font License 1.1), the Lucide icons (ISC licence) and Pyodide (MPL 2.0 licence), which runs the checks inside the browser. The metadata belong to the bodies that publish them on data.gov.gr.
terms.liability.title: Liability
terms.liability.text: The tool is provided as it is, without warranty. Its author is not liable for decisions based on the result.
terms.contact.title: Contact
terms.contact.text: For errors and suggestions, open an issue in the repository on GitHub.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.heading: The {count} criteria and how they are scored
criteria.lead: The criteria are those of the study “Quality and AI readiness of the open data of data.gov.gr”. For each of them, this page gives what it asks, when it gets 2, 1 or 0, and what the application does with it. The word “files” stands for everything a dataset offers: files, links and services.
criteria.scale.title: How to read a score
criteria.scale.scores: Every criterion gets a score of 0, 1 or 2. In the result of a check, 2 is shown as {met}, 1 as {partly} and 0 as {not_met}. When the metadata are not enough for a score, the application writes {not_measured}.
criteria.scale.kinds: The application treats every criterion in one of three ways:
criteria.kind.by_rule.text: The score comes from the rule of the criterion alone, without human judgement.
criteria.kind.proposal.text: The check sees only the metadata. The study confirms the score with a look at the dataset, and it is worth doing the same.
criteria.kind.checklist.text: The criteria that need the files themselves or human judgement get no score from the application. They appear as questions in the tab {tab} of the result, to be checked by hand.
criteria.scale.core: The core criteria are {codes}. They decide to which of the three groups of the study a dataset belongs: “Ready”, “Almost ready” or “Not yet”.
criteria.scale.high_value: {codes} apply only to the high-value datasets. These datasets are defined by Regulation (EU) 2023/138.
criteria.app.title: What the application does
criteria.app.files: The application gives no score: the criterion can only be judged by opening the files themselves, which the application does not download. It appears as a question in the tab {tab} of the result.
criteria.app.judgement: The application gives no score: the criterion needs human judgement. It appears as a question in the tab {tab} of the result.
criteria.opinion: The AI second opinion asks {n} questions about this criterion.
criteria.opinion.one: The AI second opinion asks one question about this criterion.
criteria.source.title: Where the rules come from
criteria.source.text: The rules are those of the study, version {version} of the criteria. The full text, in English, with the way every criterion is checked and its sources, is in the repository of the study.
criterion.Q1.question: Can the dataset's own resources be downloaded and opened?
criterion.Q1.score_2: Every resource can be downloaded and opens without error.
criterion.Q1.score_1: At least one resource can be downloaded and opened, but at least one other fails (broken link, error page, empty or wrong file).
criterion.Q1.score_0: No resource can be downloaded or opened.
criterion.Q2.question: How many values are missing?
criterion.Q2.score_2: Less than 5% of the cells are empty and no column is entirely empty.
criterion.Q2.score_1: 5-20% of the cells are empty, or at least one column is entirely empty.
criterion.Q2.score_0: More than 20% of the cells are empty, or no file can be opened.
criterion.Q2.not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
criterion.Q3.question: Are the values recorded in the same way throughout the dataset?
criterion.Q3.score_2: Each column has one type, format and unit, and all files of the dataset share the same structure.
criterion.Q3.score_1: Minor inconsistencies: mixed date or number formats in a column, numbers stored as text, different column names or order between files of the same dataset.
criterion.Q3.score_0: Inconsistencies that prevent analysis without manual work (e.g. values shifted between columns, different units mixed in one column), or no file can be opened.
criterion.Q3.not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
criterion.Q4.question: Are the values plausible?
criterion.Q4.score_2: No implausible values in the automatic checks and in a manual review of 10 random records.
criterion.Q4.score_1: Isolated implausible values (fewer than 1% of the records), e.g. negative counts or outliers that look like typing errors.
criterion.Q4.score_0: Systematic errors (1% of the records or more): coordinates outside Greece, dates in the future, values in the wrong columns; or no file can be opened.
criterion.Q4.not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
criterion.Q5.question: Is the dataset updated as often as its metadata declare?
criterion.Q5.score_2: Updated within the declared frequency (with one period of tolerance), or declared as not updated (one-off or historical data) with a description that says so.
criterion.Q5.score_1: The newest data are one to three periods late, or no frequency is declared but the dataset was updated in the last 12 months.
criterion.Q5.score_0: The newest data are older than three update periods, or no frequency is declared and there has been no update for more than 12 months.
criterion.Q5.how: The application compares the update frequency that the dataset declares with the newest upload of a file on the portal. With a regular frequency declared, e.g. monthly, it gives 2 when the last upload is within two periods, 1 up to four periods and 0 beyond. Without a frequency that gives a period, e.g. “irregular”, it gives 1 when a file was uploaded in the last 12 months and 0 otherwise. A dataset declared as not updated gets 2 when its title or description states the period of the data. When the portal gives no upload date, the check writes “Not measured”.
criterion.Q6.question: What is the most open format in which the data are offered?
criterion.Q6.score_2: At least one open, non-proprietary structured format (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, XML, GML, KML, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, NetCDF, RDF) or a download service in such a format (WFS, API): 3 stars or more.
criterion.Q6.score_1: Structured but vendor-specific formats (XLS, XLSX, SHP, MDB) or vendor-specific services (Esri REST): 2 stars.
criterion.Q6.score_0: Only unstructured formats (PDF, word-processor documents, images, web pages) or map views without data (WMS): 1 star.
criterion.Q6.how: The application places every file on the 5-star scale: by its declared format, failing that by the extension of its address, failing that by the media type that the link checker of the portal recorded. The dataset gets the score of its best file: 3 stars or more give 2, 2 stars give 1 and 1 star gives 0. A compressed archive is rated only when its name or address says what it holds; if no file can be rated, the check writes “Not measured”. The files themselves are not opened, so the score is a proposal.
criterion.M1.question: Are the metadata that DCAT-AP makes mandatory present and meaningful?
criterion.M1.score_2: Title, a meaningful description (at least 100 characters, saying what the data contain) and an access URL for every resource.
criterion.M1.score_1: All are present, but the description repeats the title or is shorter than 100 characters.
criterion.M1.score_0: A mandatory element is missing: title, description, or an access URL for a resource.
criterion.M1.how: The application checks that there are a title and a description and that every file has an access address. It measures the description without its HTML tags: if it has fewer than 100 characters or is the same as the title, the score is 1. If the title, the description or the address of a file is missing, the score is 0. Whether the description really says what the data contain is judged by a person, so the score is a proposal.
criterion.M2.question: How many of seven descriptive metadata are present: keyword, theme, publisher, contact point, geographical coverage, temporal coverage, update frequency?
criterion.M2.how: The application counts how many of seven details hold a value: keywords, theme, publisher, contact point, geographical coverage, temporal coverage, update frequency. Six or seven give 2, three to five give 1, two or fewer give 0. Any value counts, even a very broad one. As publisher only the field of the publisher counts, not the organisation that owns the dataset.
criterion.M3.question: Are theme, file format and update frequency given with terms of the controlled vocabularies?
criterion.M3.score_2: All of those present use controlled vocabularies.
criterion.M3.score_1: Some of them; the rest are free text.
criterion.M3.how: The application checks whether the theme, the update frequency and the format of every file are given with terms of the European vocabularies: the EU data themes, frequencies and file types, or the IANA media types. It judges only what is declared. If all are terms of the vocabularies the score is 2; if some are, 1; if none is or nothing is declared, 0. A format counts only when it matches a term exactly: “xl” or “shp zip” is free text.
criterion.M4.question: Is an open licence declared clearly for all resources?
criterion.M4.score_2: Every resource carries the same permissive licence as a term of the licence vocabulary: CC0, CC BY 4.0 or an equivalent or less restrictive open licence.
criterion.M4.score_1: An open licence, but not declared for every resource, given only as text without a link, conflicting between resources, or more restrictive than CC BY 4.0 (e.g. share-alike).
criterion.M4.score_0: No licence, or a licence that restricts re-use (non-commercial, no derivatives, permission required).
criterion.M4.how: The application reads the licence of every file, as the portal shows it. The same permissive licence (CC0, CC BY, ODC-BY or PDDL) on every file gives 2. A licence missing on some files, different licences, a share-alike licence (CC BY-SA, ODbL) or a licence given only as text gives 1. No licence, or a licence that restricts use (e.g. non-commercial only), gives 0. The licence at the level of the dataset, which the portal does not show, does not count.
criterion.M5.question: Can the data be obtained free of charge and without registration?
criterion.M5.score_2: Free of charge and without registration.
criterion.M5.score_1: Free of charge, but registration, an API key or acceptance of additional terms is required.
criterion.M5.score_0: A charge applies, or access requires an account that is not open to everyone.
criterion.M5.not_applicable: No resource delivers data and nothing points to a charge or to registration (e.g. HTTP 404, HTTP 503, an empty list).
criterion.M6.question: How are the data made available, in the order of preference of the Ministerial Decision: API, direct link, structured file, unstructured file?
criterion.M6.score_2: An API, or a stable direct link to the complete data.
criterion.M6.score_1: Files that do not give the complete data through a direct link: split into many parts, or reachable only through an intermediate page, form or map viewer.
criterion.M6.score_0: Only through a web page or an application without download, or no working access.
criterion.M6.how: The application finds how every file is offered, from its address, its declared format and the link checker of the portal: as an API or data service, as a direct link to a file, as a map view (WMS) or as a web page. The dataset takes its best mode: an API or a direct link gives 2, only map views or only web pages give 1, no address gives 0. Whether a link gives the complete data shows only when the files are downloaded, so the score is a proposal.
criterion.M7.question: Do the dataset and its resources have stable identifiers?
criterion.M7.score_2: The dataset has a stable URI and identifier, and its resources have stable links.
criterion.M7.score_1: The dataset has a stable address, but at least one resource has no address or an address that changes (new address with every upload, query or session parameters).
criterion.M7.score_0: No resource has an address, or the dataset has no resources.
criterion.M7.how: The portal gives every dataset a permanent identifier, so the application judges the addresses of the files. An address is stable when it is a file uploaded on the portal, a table of the portal, a request to a standard service or a plain address on another site. It changes when it depends on a key or on a session, or when it passes through a link shortener or a search engine. If all are stable the score is 2; if one changes or is missing, 1; if there is no address at all, 0.
criterion.M8.question: Does the dataset avoid exposing personal data?
criterion.M8.score_2: No personal data; or personal data published under a legal obligation that the metadata state; or data aggregated or anonymised, as stated.
criterion.M8.score_1: Indirect identification is possible (e.g. very small counts, exact locations linked to individuals) and the dataset does not state how it was anonymised; or personal data are published under a legal obligation that the metadata state nowhere.
criterion.M8.score_0: Personal data of natural persons (names, identity or tax numbers, home addresses, personal contact details) are published without any legal obligation.
criterion.M8.not_applicable: No file of the dataset is available, so that nothing can be inspected; the failure is counted in Q1.
criterion.M9.question: Do the metadata mark the dataset as high-value?
criterion.M9.score_2: High-value category and a reference to Regulation 2023/138 as applicable legislation.
criterion.M9.score_1: Partial marking: the category without a reference to Regulation 2023/138, the reference without the category, or only the high-value dataset type.
criterion.M9.score_0: No marking: the dataset is high-value by content only.
criterion.M9.how: The application reads three fields of the portal: the high-value category, the reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/138 and the type of the dataset. A category together with a reference to the Regulation gives 2; a partial marking, e.g. a category without the reference, gives 1. What counts is that the marking is there, not whether the category is right. For a dataset without any marking the application gives no score and writes “Not judged automatically”, because it cannot know whether its data are high-value.
criterion.M10.question: Is the dataset available both through an API and as a bulk download, as the Regulation requires?
criterion.M10.score_2: An API with public documentation and terms of use, and a bulk download of the complete dataset.
criterion.M10.score_1: Only one of the two, or an API without public documentation and terms of use.
criterion.M10.score_0: Neither an API nor a bulk download of the complete dataset.
criterion.AI1.question: Can a program read the data directly, without manual cleaning?
criterion.AI1.score_2: One header row, one record per row and one value per cell, without notes or totals inside the table; or a standard structured format (GeoJSON, JSON, XML) that is read without errors.
criterion.AI1.score_1: Readable after minor cleaning: title or note rows above the table, a totals row, numbers stored as text, a header split over two rows.
criterion.AI1.score_0: Not without manual work: PDF or scanned documents, images, spreadsheets laid out for printing (merged cells, several tables in one sheet), or no data file.
criterion.AI2.question: Is the meaning and the unit of every field documented, and are the codes explained (data dictionary)?
criterion.AI2.score_2: A written explanation gives the meaning of every field, the unit of every measure and every code or abbreviation, in the metadata, in a data dictionary, in a declared public standard, in the file itself or on a page linked from the metadata. The type of a field is not asked for separately.
criterion.AI2.score_1: Partial: the field names are clear but units or codes are not explained, or only some fields are documented.
criterion.AI2.score_0: No documentation: the meaning of the fields or codes has to be guessed.
criterion.AI2.not_applicable: The dataset has no fields: map images and documents of running text.
criterion.AI3.question: Are earlier periods or versions of the data available?
criterion.AI3.score_2: A continuous series of at least three periods or versions in the same structure: every period from the first to the last is there, with the same columns.
criterion.AI3.score_1: Some earlier periods or versions, with gaps or in a different structure; or only two periods or versions; or a single period, when the other periods are published as separate datasets of the same publisher.
criterion.AI3.score_0: Only the current state; earlier data have been replaced or removed.
criterion.AI3.not_applicable: The data have by nature no before and after: the image of the map of one act, the document of one act, a product with fixed reference years that does not recur.
criterion.AI4.question: Can the dataset be described in Croissant, or with a datasheet, from the information available?
criterion.AI4.score_2: A valid Croissant description in which every field has its type and its meaning, or, for data without records, a datasheet that states what the data contain, how they were collected and for which uses they are suitable.
criterion.AI4.score_1: A valid Croissant description whose fields are missing or do not all carry a meaning; or a datasheet with major gaps; or, where neither can be written, documentation that says more than the title about what the data contain or how they were collected.
criterion.AI4.score_0: Neither a valid Croissant description nor a datasheet can be written, and the documentation only repeats the title.
criterion.AI5.question: Can the content be split into self-contained pieces that an AI system can retrieve and cite?
criterion.AI5.score_2: Records or text passages with a stable identifier and a link to the source, in text that is extracted cleanly in UTF-8, Greek included.
criterion.AI5.score_1: Usable after conversion (text extraction from a born-digital PDF, flattening of a spreadsheet), or the pieces lack a stable identifier or a link to the source.
criterion.AI5.score_0: Not usable: scanned images or maps without text, or no content that can be extracted.
criterion.AI6.question: Can the data be joined with other datasets through common codes or coordinates?
criterion.AI6.score_2: Standard codes (e.g. municipality codes of the Kallikratis classification, NUTS or LAU codes, KAD/NACE activity codes, tax or GEMI numbers, KAEK cadastral codes) or coordinates in a declared reference system.
criterion.AI6.score_1: Only names (e.g. municipality names) or codes internal to the publisher, or coordinates without a declared reference system.
criterion.AI6.score_0: No identifiers or location information that allow linkage.
criterion.AI7.question: Do the metadata or the documentation state the known limitations of the data?
criterion.AI7.score_2: All four elements are stated: coverage, gaps, collection method, and known errors or changes of method.
criterion.AI7.score_1: One to three of the four elements are stated, e.g. only the source or only the coverage.
criterion.AI7.score_0: No statement about coverage, gaps, collection method or known errors.
